namingPolicyNotHistory: Korean map labels are editorial conventions; they do not change local official names, historical officialPeriods or the place identity.

boundary.description: Apply Korean Sino-Korean character readings for Chinese-language mainland toponyms before the 1912-01-01 founding of the Republic of China and a Chinese-pronunciation-based Korean map label from that date. This is a uniform PandoEditor editorial style change, not a city renaming or an assertion that Korean speakers immediately changed usage.
boundary.event: Founding of the Republic of China / 중화민국 건국 (1912-01-01)
boundary.geographicScope: Mainland China, for the selected Chinese-language local toponym; Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan are not automatically included.

rules.koreanLabelConvention: Korean transcription of Japanese place-name pronunciation
rules.exclude: Sino-Korean readings of Japanese place-name kanji as separate aliases (e.g. 동경 for 東京, 대판 for 大阪).
rules.historicalLocalToponyms: Respect actual historical name changes (e.g. 江戸 -> 에도, 東京 -> 도쿄).

rules.koreanLabelConvention: Sino-Korean reading of the date-appropriate selected Chinese-language local toponym
Korean rendering of Chinese pronunciation of the date-appropriate selected Chinese-language local toponym

resolutionOrder: First resolve actual local-city-name changes for the map date. Never turn a Korean map-transcription convention change into an asserted Chinese official rename.
Choose a date-appropriate local toponym from names[] using documented official naming periods when available; year-only dates remain approximate.
Apply a map-label language convention to THAT toponym, not to its present-day English name.
Use a verified koMapLabels mapping if the name is covered; otherwise hold for review rather than guessing a transliteration.
Do not derive naming language, polity or sovereignty from sourceCountryCode; this is GeoNames source metadata only.
Only one preferred Korean display name may be selected at a given date. Do not keep historical Sino-Korean readings as concurrent alternate Korean map labels after the 1912-01-01 boundary.
exceptions: For non-Mandarin Chinese-language varieties, minority-language and multilingual mainland localities, explicitly select the period's applicable local toponym and pronunciation; never infer Mandarin or sovereignty solely from a modern GeoNames CN country code. Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan are outside the automatic mainland rule and require separate consideration.
note: This policy is for future reviewed name selection, not a completed audit or runtime change. Existing 1–15 batch records, historical display transitions and deployment manifests remain unchanged until a separately approved review.
